omx-clap-host

omx-clap-host hosts CLAP and LV2 audio plugins without a screen. You drive it over a socket with the same text commands as mod-host, and each plugin appears in your JACK or PipeWire graph as a client of its own. It is for controllers, mixers and stage rigs on Linux that already talk to mod-host and want CLAP plugins beside their LV2 ones.

An LV2 plugin runs natively, through lilv in the host's own process, mapped by the LV2 adapter (libomx-clap-lv2). The CLAP hosting core is a library of its own, libomx-clap-core, for programs that host CLAP plugins themselves. The host, the core and the adapter share one version.

Install

Fedora 44 (x86_64 and aarch64):

sudo dnf install https://www.openmixer.org/rpm/openmixer-release.noarch.rpm
sudo dnf install omx-clap-host

Debian bookworm and trixie and Raspberry Pi OS (amd64 and arm64):

cd /tmp && curl -fsSLO https://www.openmixer.org/deb/openmixer-release.deb && sudo apt install ./openmixer-release.deb
sudo apt update && sudo apt install omx-clap-host

To build on the core: omx-clap-core-devel (libomx-clap-core-dev) and pkg-config --cflags --libs omx-clap-core.

Start

omx-clap-scan /usr/lib64/clap/lsp-plugins.clap      # what a CLAP file holds
omx-clap-host -n -p 5555                            # prints: omx-clap-host ready!

In another terminal (messages end in a NUL byte):

send() { printf '%s\0' "$1" | nc -w3 127.0.0.1 5555 | tr '\0' '\n'; }
send "add clap:/usr/lib64/clap/lsp-plugins.clap#in.lsp-plug.limiter_stereo 0"   # resp 0
send "add lv2:urn:zamaudio:ZamComp 1"                                          # resp 1

Each plugin is now the JACK client effect_<N>, with ports in_<k> and out_<k>.
